query: What signals suggest an agent's tickets will take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: issue_type_or_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizing tickets by issue type gives a strong grouping axis to compare resolution times across issue classes. Values are soundly derived from short_description (database access, VPN, network, software).

per_column.name: assigned_agent_or_resolver
per_column.rationale: Agent identity is central to the per-agent query, but this largely duplicates the existing assigned_to/closed_by original columns, reducing incremental value. Groundedness is plausible from those fields though the source samples shown don't include them, so it's a reasonable read.

per_column.name: issue_scope_or_impact_scale
per_column.rationale: Scope/impact is a useful axis potentially correlated with resolution time. However groundedness is weak: short_descriptions like 'Unable to access the database' or 'VPN issue' do not state whether the impact is single_user vs system_wide; these labels are largely inferred beyond textual support.

per_column.name: root_cause_mechanism_or_failure_pattern
per_column.rationale: Failure-pattern grouping is analytically useful. Some values are defensible (connectivity fault for VPN), but others overreach: 'Unable to access the database' and 'Unable to access the intranet' labeled 'server_unavailable_or_crash' assert a specific mechanism the text does not support.

per_column.name: is_recurring_or_duplicate_issue
per_column.rationale: Recurrence could plausibly relate to resolution time, but the column is near-constant (421 true / 79 false) reducing leverage, and the flag is largely unsupported: 'Unable to access the database' or 'Software update issue' give no evidence of recurrence, yet they are marked true.

per_column.name: single_agent_ownership_or_no_reassignment
per_column.rationale: Reassignment/handoff is a genuinely plausible signal for longer resolution, giving real analytical leverage. Groundedness is uncertain since the table has no reassignment history field shown; the value appears inferred rather than clearly warranted.

per_column.name: extended_time_to_final_closure_or_last_update_lag
per_column.rationale: A lag flag is directly relevant to resolution duration. But in the samples closed_at equals sys_updated_on exactly, so there is no observable lag, yet some rows are marked true; the flag appears not derivable from the available timestamps and risks circularity with the target.

per_column.name: infrastructure_dependency
per_column.rationale: This is almost a one-to-one restatement of issue_type_or_category (email->email_infrastructure, vpn->vpn_gateway), adding little new analytical axis. Values are well grounded in the descriptions.

judge.rationale: The column set provides several genuine grouping axes (issue type, scope, root cause, ownership/reassignment, closure lag) relevant to why an agent's tickets take longer, so table-level usefulness is moderately high. However, some columns dilute this: infrastructure_dependency largely restates issue_type, and assigned_agent duplicates existing original columns. Groundedness is mixed: type and infrastructure labels read soundly from short_description, but scope/impact, root-cause mechanism, recurrence, and the closure-lag flag frequently assert specifics the terse descriptions and equal-timestamp evidence do not support, indicating several confident inventions.
